claims.text: Amend P1 with a helper rule, no marker and no purity proof. A helper call is legal when the callee is an import or module-level function whose arguments are all in the closed grammar (a closure argument is a compile error). Its hole paths are the union of the argument paths, as 0001 already says. A whole-model argument is a warning. If the helper body is one return expression in the closed grammar, the analysis inlines it for exact paths, the same as partials. A hidden dependency in a helper (module state, Date.now) can only cause a stale binding, so dev mode re-evaluates each patched hole from the new model and reports a mismatch as an error naming the hole. The view-ir contract gets one line, helper: 'args' | 'inlined'.

claims.text: P6's dev re-evaluation cannot catch the failure it targets. A hidden dependency in a helper makes a hole stale because its binding is not patched, and unpatched binding chunks are not loaded, so 'each patched hole' only re-evaluates holes that were already recomputed, and the check is circular. Catching a stale hole means evaluating every hole after each update, which loads every binding chunk in dev and changes the request pattern the acceptance test counts. It also flags Date.now holes on every update as mismatches.

evidence.source: docs/roadmaps/core/contracts/compiled-format.md lines 24-29 (manifest maps binding group to chunk and path set; patch loads chunks for changed paths via diffPaths)
evidence.detail: stale = path set missed a read; the patcher never evaluates it, so a check limited to patched holes sees nothing

claims.text: Cheaper and sound check for P6: run it in the must node testing-mount, in Node tests, not in the browser. After each message in a test, re-render the whole view on the server from the new model and compare it with the DOM the patcher produced. This catches stale holes from any cause, needs no dev chunk loading, and uses code that already exists (ssr-render plus patch-bindings). Also make a whole-model argument to a helper a compile error, not a warning: its path set is the root, so the hole rebinds on every patch and defeats the goal.
